summary: No-code theory conversation across the wallet's whole surface. Walked the operator through Nostr plumbing as transport-not-identity (Phase 5c brings Tier R + remote sync; NIP-46 and recovery-cohort messaging deferred); the human-pattern application space (provably-before predictions, mutually-held contracts/consents, birth-to-death life threads, witness-converging historical evidence, selective professional credentialing, object provenance, kin recognition, community-as-living-organism, the entire ritual cluster); the honest comparable-systems landscape (PGP web-of-trust as the 35-year-old grandparent, Keybase as the abandoned closest consumer ancestor, W3C VC / EU eIDAS 2.0 as institutional cousin, EAS as closest live attestation substrate, Nostr as transport substrate, DynastyTrust as direct lineage); adoption strategy (selfish use case necessary but not sufficient; eight strategic recommendations recorded); the supply-chain expansion (Phase 2.6 custody-handoff IS supply-chain handoff mathematically; ten concrete applications walked, plus B2B revenue path that doesn't compromise sovereignty). Operator's wife surfaced the load-bearing adoption test: 'how is this not just trusting the wallet?' Answered with the math-not-trust thesis grounded in the existing /verify route — paste a proof, tamper one character of the disclosed value, watch the green Proof-is-valid panel flip to amber Proof-did-NOT-verify because the leaf hash no longer matches the signed merkle root. Operator confirmed the demonstration landed.

why.text: Operator opening: 'Read everything about our wallet and I have some questions about implementations and just theory no code changes.' The session is a strategic-thinking session, not a build session — the operator is consolidating his own understanding of what's been built, what's possible, and what's next, with the wife-as-skeptic test as the most valuable adoption signal that came out of it.
